description: List size and len give the list's length, as Java and Rust spell them
isEmpty and isNotEmpty follow a queue as it is pushed
code:
queue = []
idle = queue.isEmpty()
busy = queue.isNotEmpty()
queue.push("job")
[idle, busy]

description: Rust's is_empty tests a list, and the rule follows a later pop
A string's length() method gives its character count, as Java writes it
Strings answer isEmpty, is_empty and isNotEmpty
A class population's size counts its instances and follows new ones
code:
class Order(item):
    this.item = item
orders = Order.size()
Order("tea")
Order("cake")
orders

description: A class without instances is empty and has size 0
A class-level rule tests each instance's list with isEmpty
code:
class Bin(items):
    this.items = items
$Bin.empty = $Bin.items.isEmpty()
full = Bin([1])
spare = Bin([])
full.items.pop()
[full.empty, spare.empty]

description: Arguments of a size alias are evaluated and ignored, as length() treats them
On a class name the population alias wins over an instance method of the same name
code:
class Box:
    def size() => 99
b = Box()
[b.size(), Box.size()]

description: A failed update through an alias rolls back, so the rule keeps its value
code:
stock = ["bolt"]
low = stock.size() < 2
failure = ""
try:
    stock = 7
catch error:
    failure = error
[stock, low, failure]

description: A program that caught the former alias error now receives the size
code:
xs = [1, 2]
try:
    r = xs.size()
catch e:
    r = "caught"
r

description: Templates and conditional expressions read the aliases
code:
jobs = ["a", "b"]
label = `${jobs.size()} jobs`
state = jobs.isEmpty() ? "idle" : "busy"
[label, state]

description: Counting the empty shelves of a population with filter, isEmpty and size
code:
class Shelf(items):
    this.items = items
Shelf([])
Shelf([1])
Shelf([])
Shelf.filter(shelf -> shelf.items.isEmpty()).size()
